title: Phrasal Verbs with Off, On, Over, Up

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small word like to, for, on, off that shows place, direction or relation

vocabulary.example: We have to call off tomorrow's meeting.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to accept more work or responsibility
vocabulary.example: The boss asked me to take on a new account.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to have a good relationship with someone
vocabulary.note_ar: في أمريكا أكثر: get along with
vocabulary.example: I get on well with my colleagues.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to need something or someone in order to work or happen
to review something in detail and talk about it
vocabulary.example: Let's go over the report together.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to search for information in a book or online
vocabulary.example: Look up the word in a dictionary.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to contact someone again to give or get more information
vocabulary.example: I'll follow up with the client next week.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to continue for longer than needed
vocabulary.example: The meeting dragged on for three hours.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to talk about your personal feelings or private life
vocabulary.example: He finally opened up about his problems.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to wear smart clothes; to make something look better
vocabulary.example: We need to dress up this presentation a little.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to consider something carefully before deciding
vocabulary.example: Take the weekend to think it over.

vocabulary.meaning_en: long, heavy and not comfortable to use
vocabulary.example: That sentence is cumbersome; use a phrasal verb.

fine_lines.title: Meanings of the prepositions
fine_lines.explanation_ar: off: ابتعاد أو انفصال (call off). on: التصاق أو إضافة أو استمرار (take on, drag on). over: تفكير وتواصل (go over, think over). up: تجميع، اقتراب، إكمال، تحسين (look up, follow up, dress up).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Off: moving away, detaching (call off). On: touching, adding, continuing (take on, drag on). Over: considering, communicating (go over). Up: collecting, approaching, completing, improving (look up, dress up).

expressions.phrase: I have to call off the meeting.
expressions.meaning_en: I have to cancel the meeting.
expressions.example: Sorry, I have to call off the 8 a.m. meeting.
Bring the contract and let's go over it together.

expressions.meaning_en: I'll contact you again later with more information.
expressions.example: I'll follow up with you on Monday.

expressions.meaning_en: They don't have a good relationship.
expressions.example: I heard you two don't get on.

expressions.meaning_en: It is not sure; it needs...
expressions.example: That depends on who you spoke to.

grammar.title: Verb + preposition = new meaning
grammar.explanation_ar: في الفعل المركّب يحتفظ الفعل بجزء من معناه، لكن حرف الجر يغيّر المعنى العام: call (يتصل) + off (ابتعاد) = call off (يُلغي). take (يأخذ) + on (إضافة) = take on (يتولّى عملًا إضافيًا). والأفعال المركّبة تقول الكثير بكلمات أقل.
grammar.explanation_en: In a phrasal verb, the verb keeps part of its meaning, but the preposition changes the overall meaning: call + off = cancel; take + on = accept more work. Phrasal verbs say more with fewer words.
examples: I have to cancel the meeting. → I have to call off the meeting.
Accept more work → take on more work
Review it in detail → go over it

choices: I have to call off the meeting.

"She wants me to ___ the report with you." (review in detail)
"I heard you two don't ___." (have a good relationship)
questions.explanation_en: Get on = have a good relationship.

questions.question: "Let me ___ the word in the dictionary."
"The meeting ___ for three hours." (longer than needed)
questions.explanation_en: Drag on = go on too long.
